title: Pill — The box measures. Pill explains.

slides.name: Title

els.text: CAL HACKS 13.0 · IDEA TO DEMO · FIGMA
A box of hobby parts around an Arduino UNO Q. One whole tablet in a small cup, a 60-second quick run, one of three answers. In a clinic, that answer decides whether the supplier gets paid.
Art · the site’s binary pill (pill.js), captured from pill-site.vercel.app

slides.notes: Pill is a box of hobby parts around an Arduino UNO Q. One whole tablet in a small cup, a sixty-second quick run, two light sensors. It says three things only: PASS, NEEDS LAB, UNABLE TO VERIFY.

slides.name: The moment

els.text: THE MOMENT · DELIVERY D-1042 · REPLAY TM-02

Clinic app replay of its simulated two-channel design. The bottle says vitamin B2. The blue line drops into the reference band, so a one-sensor tester would call it a pass. The 90° channel never moves.
Illustration · the shape of replay TM-02, redrawn; not live sensor data.
RULE N2 · INLINE MOVED, 90° DID NOT RISE
A one-sensor tester would have passed it.
POLICY P2 · HOLD, DRAFT THE LAB REFERRAL

slides.notes: This is the clinic app replaying its simulated two-channel design. The bottle says vitamin B2; inside is chalk. The blue line drops right into the reference band, so a one-sensor tester would call that a pass, but the 90-degree channel never moves. Pill says NEEDS LAB and the supplier's four hundred and eighty dollars stays held, lab referral drafted. Sandbox money; this is a replay, and we say so.

slides.name: The problem

els.text: WHO estimates 1 in 10 medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified. The lab instrument that catches one costs $20,000 to $100,000.
Illustration · one tablet in ten. WHO, 2017: substandard and falsified products counted together.
extra malaria deaths a year in sub-Saharan Africa, modelled central estimate, from substandard and falsified antimalarials (range 64,000–158,000)
children's deaths linked to contaminated cough syrups in three countries, 2022–23, most under five
spent each year on substandard and falsified medical products, by WHO's estimate

slides.notes: WHO estimates 1 in 10 medical products in low- and middle-income countries is substandard or falsified. A new lab dissolution tester costs twenty to a hundred thousand dollars, and lab results take seven to ten business days. A clinic pharmacist has neither; what they have is an invoice to pay this afternoon.

slides.name: The station

els.text: Lot numbers can be copied. Dissolution cannot.
A recall lookup trusts the label. Pill measures the tablet itself: one tablet in a cup of water inside a dark chamber, two light sensors watching it dissolve.
Two photoresistors in 10 kΩ dividers from the 3V3 pin: A0 across the cup, A1 at 90° to the beam.
All LEDs off, both sensors read. Room light cancels out of the signal instead of leaking into it.
Each LED lights alone and both sensors read again: light that gets through, light that scatters sideways.
ms, dark, blue, white, red for each sensor, at 115200 baud. The firmware decides nothing.
Photo · purple 3D-printed chamber, clear cup of water; side box with white, blue and red LEDs; the UNO Q at left.
Photo · from above: blue light inside the cup, the LED box below it, the UNO Q at lower left.
Drawing · the chamber design, top view (pillgate/diagrams): the LED pod on one side, one photoresistor straight across the cup, one at 90° to the beam.

slides.notes: The station is an Arduino UNO Q, a 3.3-volt board with a 12-bit ADC. These are photos of it from Saturday: a purple 3D-printed chamber holding a clear cup of water, a side box with white, blue and red LEDs, and the UNO Q next to it. The drawing shows where the two photoresistors sit, one in line with the beam and one at ninety degrees. Once a second it turns every LED off and reads both, the dark reading that cancels room light, then lights blue, white and red in turn and reads again. It sends one CSV line a second. The firmware decides nothing; the laptop does the maths.

slides.name: The station app

els.text: Pill Gate runs on the laptop next to the box (Python, FastAPI). It guides the check and compares the run with a reference profile built from three or more runs of a known-good tablet.
Lid closed, the LED reaches the sensor.
The blank must hold steady for 10 s.
The lid opening on both sensors marks the start.
THREE ANSWERS, WRITTEN THIS WAY IN THE STATION APP
Time-to-80 % and final colour inside the spread of the reference runs.
Outside it: slower, weaker, cloudier or clearer than the reference.
No reference for this product, lid open too long, a noisy blank, or the curve never settled.

slides.notes: The station has its own app, Pill Gate, on the laptop beside the box. Prepare checks the lid and the light path, ten seconds of clean water make the blank, the lid opening marks the tablet going in, sixty seconds of dissolving, then the result. It compares the run with a reference profile from three or more runs of a known-good tablet, and it says one of three things: Passed the screen, Needs lab testing, or Unable to verify.

slides.name: How a run works

els.text: Quick mode stops 60 s after the tablet goes in; full mode runs 2–10 min until the curve is flat. The station app compares the run with a reference profile (three or more good runs); the clinic app draws it as a pill filling to its reference plateau.
0:00 · dark, then 10 s of clean water. Lid open? No run.
One whole tablet in; stirred by hand.
The light through the cup changes as it dissolves.
Illustration · example levels; the app draws them live from the sensor stream.

slides.notes: One whole tablet in a small cup, stirred by hand. Quick mode is sixty seconds after the tablet goes in; full mode runs two to ten minutes until the curve is flat. The run is compared with a reference, and the answer is one of three. A model explains the result in plain English but never sets it.

slides.name: Three answers

els.text: Seven rules, checked in order. A model writes the plain-English “why”; it never sets the verdict.
Plateau in the reference band and the 90° channel rose with it (P1).
Light dropped with no rise at 90°, no plateau, or a plateau outside the band (N1–N3).
No reference for this drug, a fault, or too little data (U1–U3).

slides.notes: It says three things only: PASS, NEEDS LAB, UNABLE TO VERIFY. Never a fourth. In the clinic app PASS means this tablet's curve matched the reference band; it does not mean right drug, right dose or contaminant-free.

Blue · white · red LEDs, 2 photoresistors, 1 CSV line/s. The firmware decides nothing.
Three answers, never four. No model sets a verdict.

Claude may only return the ceiling or escalate.

Release · passed + no recall + within cap + tap

Escalate · unable to verify → a person; nothing moves

Buyer agent · another clinic, or an agent with no local reference

Real 402 today; the facilitator’s verify step answered (insufficient_balance on our unfunded test wallet). @x402/express · @x402/evm · CDP SDK. Service modes cdp · public-facilitator · simulated, each named in every response.
Station: reads the bottle label + imprint, writes the report, answers Ask, behind the guardrail. Clinic: the two-sentence “why”; the escrow clerk (returns the ceiling computed in code, or escalate).
Clinic: reads the bottle label into editable fields (unreadable → null); runs the agentic checker (label, up to three cup frames, code tools for the recall lookup).
Sets a verdict; invents a field

analysis.py and rules.ts (U1 U2 U3 N1 N2 N3 P1) set every verdict; the policy computes the ceiling; the clause filter drops any model sentence with a banned claim word (over half dropped → rule text).

slides.notes: How the money moves, and who decides. One tablet goes into the station; deterministic code turns the curve into one of three answers. The policy agent runs six clauses in code to get a ceiling; Claude may only return that ceiling or escalate. Passed, no recall, within the cap and a pharmacist’s tap releases the escrow to the supplier; Needs lab holds it and drafts a lab referral; Unable to verify escalates to a person. The money column is three Coinbase CDP server wallets, USDC on Base Sepolia, testnet, and escrow moves are simulated until we have a CDP key. Underneath, another clinic can buy a verdict over x402: the 402 is real today, the paid 200 is still pending. Claude and Gemini explain and read; code sets every verdict.

slides.name: App screens

els.text: The clinic app: on a laptop and a phone.
25 routes in React. All 364 app screenshots go into the Design file, one frame each, labelled with their route. These twelve are the newest pass.

slides.notes: The clinic app is one web app on a laptop and on any phone. These are the newest build pass; the Design file has every screenshot, grouped by pass and linked to its route.

slides.name: Six phases

els.text: THE CLINIC APP, PHASE BY PHASE
The clinic app’s run, live against its simulated station. Each phase has its own time, its own look and its own check; a failed check stops the run and says why.
LEDs off. The box must read dark; a light leak means the lid is open, and the run stops.
Plain water. The blank must hold steady (CV under 2 %) or it retries, up to 3 times.
It waits for the inline reading to fall 6 %. After 30 s the screen prompts.
The pill fills, the curve falls, the 90° channel rises. Flat at 90° while blue falls: the amber moment.
Flat for 20 s (|dA/dt| < ε) means plateau. No plateau by 180 s: timeout.
Seven rules, in order. The rule that fired is printed with the word.

slides.notes: The clinic app shows a run as six phases, played here against its simulated station. Lights off for three seconds: the box must be dark, or the lid is open and nothing runs. Ten seconds of clear water as the blank; it must be steady. Drop the tablet; it waits for the reading to fall six percent. Dissolving: the pill fills and the 90-degree channel should rise with it. Settling: twenty flat seconds is a plateau. Then the seven rules give the word.

slides.name: Gemini checker

els.text: Gemini checks what the sensor says.
After the run, Gemini reads the label, looks at the cup and checks for a recall, then compares that with the sensor. Six steps, each logged with its own time.
The sensor decides. The checker explains and never changes the word. A pharmacist or doctor decides.

slides.notes: After the run, a Gemini agent checks what the sensor says: it reads the label, looks at photos of the cup, checks openFDA for a recall, cross-checks expiry, drug and lot, and compares what the camera saw with the sensor numbers. Every step is logged with its own time. The verdict word comes from the sensor and is never changed. The follower is the same Gemini, docked on every screen, answering questions about what is on it.

slides.name: Website

els.text: Built code-first (Vite + anime.js) after a 16-persona panel scored a plain, honest page 8.0 against a copied storytelling site at 3.7. Words stay ink; colour lives in backgrounds and lines.
Hero · the binary pill, drawn in characters by pill.js
Fig 3 · three answers, the same screen as the app
Payments · the verdict is the invoice

slides.name: Workflow

els.text: Code first, then Figma from the code.
Honest order: no Figma was used Friday or Saturday morning. The Figma files are generated from the repo, and the log says so.

slides.notes: We are a code-first team. Ideation and prototyping happened in markdown, AI panels and HTML. Figma enters as the place the repo is published to: slides, screens, tokens and the ideation board.

slides.name: Design from code

els.text: screenshots · CSS :root · debate JSON · stage log
Node, no npm deps; ffmpeg for images
slides, pages and board in one file
the loop: Figma styles and variables → Composio → CSS back in the repo

Recipe for code-first teams: keep the repo as the source of truth, emit one JSON, let a plugin draw it. One run gives designers editable layers, every screen, the tokens as styles, and a board of how you decided.
Why a plugin: the Figma REST API and our Composio connector can read, comment and set variables, but cannot create layers or slides. The Plugin API can.

slides.notes: The REST API cannot draw, so the repo emits deck.json and a one-file plugin draws it in Slides, Design or FigJam. Composio closes the loop: comments, dev resources back to the code, thumbnails, and tokens back to CSS. Nobody has run it in real Figma yet; that step is marked pending.

slides.name: What PASS does not mean

els.text: The dissolution curve of this one tablet, on this box, was consistent with the reference runs. No red flags found.
That the tablet is the right drug, the right dose, or free of contaminants. Anything Pill cannot compare goes to a lab, by design.
Arduino UNO Q, 2 photoresistors, blue/white/red LEDs; one CSV line a second. One real aspirin run recorded Saturday. Reference profile not yet recorded; water-only control not yet run.
Analysis, guided run, lid detection, guardrail; 14 tests pass. Live Claude scan ran Sat 19:19 on scan_1024_191752_f0c2 (replay of the real aspirin run): Unable to verify, no reference profile yet.
Synthetic curves (B2-07, TM-02, B2-LID, AMX-01), labelled REPLAY on screen; the week of history is fixture data.
USDC escrow simulated until a CDP key. x402: real 402 and signature check; paid 200 pending. Nessie mirror built, not run. SANDBOX / TESTNET only.

slides.notes: Say the limits before a judge asks. PASS, or Passed the screen in the station app, means this tablet dissolved like the reference runs; it never calls a medicine good or bad. Then what is real today: the UNO Q station and its app are real, and a live Claude scan ran Saturday at 19:19 on a replay of our real aspirin run; there is no reference profile yet, so it said Unable to verify, and the water-only control has not run. The clinic app replays labelled synthetic curves, escrow is simulated until a CDP key, and the paid x402 200 is pending. All money is SANDBOX or TESTNET.

Three or more runs of a known-good aspirin tablet, then the water-only control against it.

rows.label: What we did
cells: Nine ideas considered, six through scored panels. FloodToll, DripGuard and Payout died on buildability or business. Lot beat Bill and Streets 13 votes of 16 and became Pill. A second panel scored a plain, honest website 8.0 against a copied storytelling site at 3.7.

The prototype was the product. The site's phone mock loops calibration, bottle, recall, run, verdict and release; those loops became APP-PLAN's twelve screens. The binary pill was tried as one HTML file before it went on the site. The clickable Figma prototype (Welcome → Run → NEEDS LAB → held → Pay) is generated by the plugin from the shipped screens, so it always matches the code; link: [fill after running].

The site's 27 tokens seeded the app's palette. The plugin puts the app's colour tokens into Figma as styles and variables, and the script reads them back as CSS, so a change made in Figma can land in code.

The clinic app (25 routes), the x402 payment service (a Nessie sandbox mirror is built, not run) and the Claude and Gemini wiring were generated against written plans. Then the repo generated its Figma: build-deck.mjs turns screenshots, site art, CSS tokens, debate JSON and this log into deck.json; the plugin draws the Slides deck, the Design pages and the FigJam board.

rows.label: What broke
cells: Plain-page scores had a standard deviation of 0: sixteen voices, one opinion. Two persona replies failed to parse. Nothing visual existed; the FigJam board was built from the JSON afterwards, not used live.

Nobody without a code editor could change or click through the prototype; the Figma Make prompt is written to fill that gap. The site went through four versions in 53 minutes; v4 moved colour off the words.

By hand, 8 of 27 tokens arrived identical, 7 changed value (some on purpose: verdict colours re-pointed at mint, amber, grey) and 12 were renamed or dropped. Nothing recorded which changes were intended. Composio's Figma tools read, comment and set variables but cannot draw a layer.

The scaffold's P6 rule held money only when the recall lookup was unreachable, so a delivery with no bottle attached could be proposed for release; a builder's end-to-end test caught it. A tail -6 cut off Vercel's output, the deploy was re-run, and we got two identical production deploys. The REST API cannot create nodes, hence a plugin.
